clashes.quote_a: Use git for Variance local code operations, including branches, commits, push, pull, merge, and rebase.
clashes.quote_b: Use MCP for Variance remote writes such as issues, PRs, project items, sub-issue links, and reviews.
clashes.situation: When pushing a feature branch to GitHub, following R228 with git push breaks R229 if its remote-write requirement includes Git-remote updates rather than only GitHub metadata writes.

clashes.quote_b: Before requesting Variance job logs, obtain the job ID from actions_list with list_workflow_jobs and the run ID.

notes: Reviewed all four folders using only the supplied rules file, grouping pushing/commits, PRs/reviews, merges, branches/worktrees, pruning/cloning/submodules, and tool routing; no scripts or APIs were used. The five sure clashes read R230's remote/project reads literally: live issue searches/lists, label checks, and workflow-job lookups are remote reads, but their specific rules require different tools. R246 explicitly permits MCP for PR-detail reads, so R230/R246 and the programmatic-detail case R230/R247 were excluded; the explicit CLI alternatives R245 and R250 were also excluded. R228/R229 is unsure because Git-remote updates may be outside the metadata-write category intended by R229. The two pruning candidates are unsure because the file does not define whether firmware sources count as non-gateware, or explicitly identify R78's preservation list as an exception to the broad deletion rules; if that list is intended as the explicit preservation exception, those candidates disappear. No clashes were found in agenta or SudokuQuest: choosing worktree isolation satisfies both the strict requirement and the isolate-or-pause alternative, single-file edits have an explicit exemption, and R48 explicitly waives the ordinary review gate for implementall sweeps. Starting stacked work and later merging it only after its base are different stages, and already available pushed-type work is not the blocked work that R95 defers. Rules saying to prune after cloning do not require pruning immediately while readers are active. Clone-local no-commit rules were kept separate from catalogue-repository commits. R101's version-control wording was not stretched into a founder-only restriction on every git operation, given its explicit reference to the root version file.
